chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Abu Basir and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who bequeathed a 'part' of his wealth, he said: 'A part is one of ten,' and he said: 'The mountains were ten.'
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'a part' (juz') mean in Islamic inheritance law according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the ambiguity of the term 'part' (juz') in bequests by defining it as one-tenth, supported by the metaphor of the ten mountains. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of interpreting vague terms in wills to prevent disputes among heirs, establishing a clear standard for fractional inheritance. The reference to 'ten mountains' serves as a mnemonic and conceptual anchor for the number ten in Arabic rhetorical tradition.
